h1: Choosing brand colors your team can actually use
p: A practical way to build a palette that works on screens, in slides and on a shipping box.
A beautiful palette that only works on a moodboard is not a palette. It is a screenshot.
We test every color on a website, a slide, a social post and a printed box before we sign it off. Colors that fail on one surface get adjusted or dropped.
Each color gets a clear role: background, text, action or accent. When the team knows what each color is for, they stop inventing new ones.

/journal/how-we-plan-a-website-before-de.title: How we plan a website before designing a single page | Synthweb Studio
/journal/how-we-plan-a-website-before-de.description: Sitemaps, content audits and wireframes: the unglamorous week that saves every project a month.
h1: How we plan a website before designing a single page
h2: Start with the pages, not the pixels
p: Sitemaps, content audits and wireframes: the unglamorous week that saves every project a month.
Most website projects that go wrong do not go wrong in design. They go wrong in the first week, when nobody agrees on what the site is for.
Before we open a design file we write a sitemap and a one-line job for every page. If a page has no job, it does not get built. This alone usually cuts a site by a third.

Next we outline the content of each page with the client: headlines, sections and the one action we want a visitor to take. Wireframes come after that, and they are fast because the hard decisions are already made.
It feels slow for a week. It saves a month.
